evidence: One inconsistent count target found among 31 criterion descriptions (3 gate, 23 functional, 2 polish, 3 visual). Frozen task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:110, cw_replace_all_atomic, says 'at least four literal matches' but then 'Require exactly the four intended replacements'. Permitted setup counts of five or more therefore have a different correct Replace all outcome than the literal four-replacement bar. Public task/environment/instructions/ui.md:11 requires Replace all, not a four-replacement limit. The app_context.md:5-7 and functional prompt.md:5,9 do not resolve the count conflict. Other explicit exceptions set a coherent scope: polish judge.toml:23 grades offered controls, render/constraints describe conjunctive outcomes, functional judge.toml:182 permits a static last-good picture, :209 distinguishes restart-tool evidence gaps, and visual descriptions :24/:34/:44 have one top anchor each. No additional row-33 defect observed. All frozen task and rule hashes match manifest; functional judge SHA256 ae1de09737223ed784057de4178b3db0b9782c99f1c88aa673f8e994e3b494e5. Raw-index artifacts matched their hashes, but no runtime evidence is used to claim this source-language conflict was executed by a judge.
counterexample: Choose valid source const values = ['R33','R33','R33','R33','R33','r33']; with Find R33 and replacement DONE. This has five case-sensitive matches and one differently cased near-match, satisfying the permitted 'at least four' setup. A conforming Replace all yields five DONE strings and unchanged r33, but can fail the stated exactly-four result. Conversely an implementation that replaces only the first four and offers atomic Undo/Redo can satisfy the count reading while leaving the fifth R33 unchanged. This is a reasoned counterexample, not an executed configured judge result.
suggested_fix: Use exactly four literal matches in the fixture, or record the initial match count N and require exactly N replacements with no original match remaining; retain the near-match and atomic Undo/Redo checks.
